title: 170 of 1,645 Lovable-built apps found exposing user data through missing row-level security
summary: Developer Matt Palmer found that Lovable, an AI service for building web apps, sometimes generated Supabase-backed apps without row-level security, leaving user data readable by anyone; on one Lovable-built site, Linkable, the email addresses of about 500 users were exposed. Scanning 1,645 Lovable-built apps he found 170 with the same flaw, exposing names, email addresses, financial information and API keys; Lovable said it had taken measures, but the article reports these did not check the generated code's correctness and the problem was not substantially resolved as of May 29, 2025.
verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17; GIGAZINE page dated Jun 02, 2025 confirms Palmer's finding, the 1,645 scanned / 170 affected figures, the roughly 500 exposed Linkable emails, and the criticism that Lovable's measures did not check code correctness. Kind set to incident rather than the sweep's disclosure: the report is by a third-party researcher and user data was exposed in production.
